chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Kinji from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban ibn Uthman from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the deceased who has hair on him, so can it be shaved off or clipped? He (peace be upon him) said: Do not touch anything from him. Wash him and bury him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on cutting the hair or nails of the deceased in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of preserving the natural state of the deceased, prohibiting the cutting of hair or nails to maintain bodily integrity until burial. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that grooming is a post-mortem act of adornment or preparation distinct from the ritual washing (Ghusl), which is performed separately. The ruling underscores the dignity of the body as a trust returned to God, untouched by human alteration after the soul's departure.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Kindy, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan Al Maysami, from Aban Bin Usman, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Abdullah who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the decease who happens to have the hair upon him, so can it be shaved off from it or clipped?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not touch anything from him. Wash him and bury him’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al-Kindiy from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan al-Mithamiy from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu ‘Abd Allah who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a dead person whose body has hairs if it is required to shave or trim them. He (the Imam) said, ‘Nothing as such must be touched. Just give him Ghusl (bath) and bury.’”
